author: Lao Tzu
pd_statement: The Tao Te Ching (in Legge’s spelling, The Tâo Teh King) is traditionally attributed to Lao Tzu. This edition uses the English translation by James Legge (1815–1897), first published in 1891 in The Sacred Books of the East, which is in the public domain. Legge’s wording, his numbering of the verses and his words in round brackets are kept; obvious printing errors are corrected.

headline: Yield and overcome.
Be still and know.
Let things flow.
paras: For more than two thousand years, eighty-one short chapters have taught readers how water wears down stone, why the softest things overcome the hardest, and how a person can act without forcing. The Tao Te Ching is one of the most translated books in the world.

This beautifully designed annotated edition presents the complete text in James Legge’s classic translation and adds what today’s reader needs: a clear guide to Taoist ideas, a plain-language note and a small practice for every chapter, and a guided 30-day practice.
